collect.bio: Édouard Philippe (born 1970) is a French centre-right politician and founder of Horizons (2021). He was Prime Minister under Emmanuel Macron from May 2017 to July 2020 and has been mayor of Le Havre since 2020, re-elected in March 2026. He announced his 2027 presidential candidacy in 2024 and launched his campaign on 5 July 2026 (slogan "Croire en nous"). He left the Horizons presidency on 9 September 2026 to build a broader coalition; Christophe Béchu took over on 1 October 2026.

offices.office: Mayor of Le Havre (second term, re-elected 2026-03-28)
President of Le Havre Seine Métropole

legal.case: Judicial investigation (Cour de justice de la République) into Covid-19 pandemic management, opened 7 July 2020; his home was searched on 15 October 2020. His current status in 2026 (témoin assisté, mis en examen, cleared) could NOT be verified. No conviction known.
HATVP censure in 2014 for opacity of his asset declaration (property values and legal fees). Administrative finding, not a criminal case.

verify.bio: Édouard Philippe (born 1970) is a French centre-right politician and founder of Horizons (2021). He was Prime Minister under Emmanuel Macron from May 2017 to July 2020 and has been mayor of Le Havre since 2020, re-elected in March 2026. He announced his 2027 presidential candidacy in September 2024 and launched his campaign on 5 July 2026 (slogan "Croire en nous"). On 9 September 2026 he announced he would leave the Horizons presidency to build a broader coalition, and Christophe Béchu took over on 1 October 2026.

offices.office: Mayor of Le Havre (second term, re-elected 2026-03-28)
President of Le Havre Seine Métropole

legal.case: Cour de justice de la République judicial investigation into Covid-19 pandemic management (opened 7 July 2020; his home was searched on 15 October 2020). He was placed under the status of témoin assisté (assisted witness) for 'abstention de combattre un sinistre' (failure to act against a disaster), not mis en examen, and the CJR's investigating commission issued a non-lieu (dismissal) for Philippe, Agnès Buzyn and Olivier Véran on 7 July 2025. Never charged or convicted.

In 2014 the HATVP (the transparency authority) published a critical assessment of his asset declaration because of omissions, and he later filed an updated declaration. This was an administrative finding and not a criminal case.

reversals.topic: PMA (medically assisted reproduction for all women)
reversals.after: As PM he carried Macron's campaign pledge and said he had 'evolved on this question'.

delivery.what: 2020 pension reform (universal points system): the government used Article 49.3 at first reading in the Assemblée nationale (29 February 2020), then suspended the reform in March 2020 because of Covid. It was never adopted.
delivery.assessment: Summary-level only. The source records the 49.3 use and his later support for raising the retirement age (65-67). No balanced assessment from sources of different leanings was obtained.

delivery.what: Government of Philippe II (21 June 2017 to 3 July 2020): labour-code ordinances, laws and budgets
delivery.assessment: The page lists ordinances and laws, but the detail could not be retrieved. No cross-leaning assessments were obtained.

delivery.what: 80 km/h speed limit on secondary roads (July 2018), which he championed personally
delivery.assessment: The source says he pushed it against Macron's preference and that it may have fed Gilets jaunes tensions. No cross-leaning assessment was obtained.

verify.sources_note: The WebSearch quota was exhausted in both the research and verification passes. All facts come from French Wikipedia pages that were opened and re-checked during verification: Édouard Philippe, Horizons, Gouvernement Philippe II and Cour de justice de la République. The CJR page cites a franceinfo article of 7 July 2025 for the non-lieu, but its URL could not be opened, so it is not cited directly. The profile is thin. It lacks cross-leaning outlets, the Horizons/2027 programme, trait corroboration and media portrayal, so the research should be re-run with search quota available. executive_experience_years counts mayor 2010-10 to 2017-05 (about 6.6 years), PM 2017-05 to 2020-07 (about 3.1) and mayor 2020-07 to 2026-10 (about 6.25), roughly 15.9 years in total. The metropole presidency overlaps the mayoralty and is not double-counted.
